baseline.name: Journal of Open Source Software
baseline.scope_notes: Peer-reviewed papers about mature research software; requires more than six months of active public development and demonstrated research use, which may be by the developers. External community adoption is a positive signal, not mandatory. Pre-trained models, notebooks, thin API clients and one-off tools are outside scope. Humans must make core design decisions and validate AI-assisted work.

route.conditions:
No fees to submit or publish. Requires mature, research-used software under an OSI-approved license, tests, documentation and more than six months of active public development. A major contributor submits, participates in public review and archives a tagged release with a DOI. AI assistance requires disclosure and human validation; AI-mediated author/editor or reviewer conversation is prohibited except translation. Models, notebooks, thin API clients and one-off analysis tools are outside scope.
No submission or publication fees. Software must meet research-impact, feature-completeness and open-development gates, including more than six months of active public development under current pre-review criteria. Major-contributor authors participate through GitHub; archive the reviewed release with a DOI using a free archive. Disclose AI tools, use and human validation. AI use in conversational interactions between authors and editors/reviewers is prohibited except translation. Human authors must make core design decisions and take responsibility.
Journal states no fees for manuscript processing or publishing and zero publication fees. Research software must satisfy submission requirements.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None in the journal submission/publication policy. Repository hosting must permit free public access; free supported archive choices exist. Existing software development expenses are not journal charges.

fee_evidence.note: Explicitly excludes submission and publication fees and documents public-development maturity, research impact, AI limits, open hosting, public review and archived-release requirements.
